record.paper_title: Basic kinetic wealth-exchange models: common features and open problems
record.context_brief: General stationary Gamma solution for KWEMs
record.original_question: For the basic homogeneous kinetic wealth-exchange models reviewed in the paper, including the A1, A2, B, C, and D models, can one derive a general analytical stationary solution that explains why the equilibrium wealth distribution is so often well fitted by a Gamma distribution, proves when that Gamma distribution is genuinely stationary, and clarifies the mechanism by which it emerges from the microscopic exchange rules rather than merely appearing as an empirical fit?

evidence.quote: The close analogies among the various models are evident, however the existence of a general solution has not been demonstrated, see e.g. Refs. [23, 41].
However, a general demonstration that the Γ-distribution is the stationary solution of KWEMs and an understanding of how it arises is still missing

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the class of basic homogeneous kinetic wealth-exchange models defined as follows. A population of $N$ agents holds nonnegative real wealths $x_1,\dots,x_N$ with fixed total $\sum_i x_i = N\langle x\rangle$. At each microscopic step, a pair $(i,j)$ is chosen at random and their wealths are updated by a conservative exchange rule $x_i + x_j = x_i' + x_j'$, in one of the following variants:

(A1) Pure random reshuffling: $x_i' = \epsilon(x_i+x_j)$, $x_j' = (1-\epsilon)(x_i+x_j)$ with $\epsilon\sim U(0,1)$.

(A2) Random reshuffling with a uniform global saving propensity $\lambda\in[0,1)$: $x_i' = \lambda x_i + \epsilon(1-\lambda)(x_i+x_j)$, $x_j' = \lambda x_j + (1-\epsilon)(1-\lambda)(x_i+x_j)$.

(B) Heterogeneous saving propensities: each agent $i$ has an individual $\lambda_i\in[0,1)$ drawn from a fixed distribution, with the same update rule as in (A2) but using $\lambda_i,\lambda_j$.

(C) Models with a multiplicative random "exchanged fraction" version of the above rules.

(D) Models with additive noise terms preserving total wealth on average.

Numerical simulations indicate that the stationary single-agent wealth distribution $f(x)$ for these models is, in many parameter regimes, well fitted by a Gamma density
$$f(x) = \frac{1}{\Gamma(\alpha)\theta^\alpha} x^{\alpha-1} e^{-x/\theta},\qquad x\ge 0,$$
with shape $\alpha$ and scale $\theta$ depending on the saving parameters.

Problem: Provide a unified analytical treatment of the models (A1), (A2), (B), (C), (D) that
(i) derives the exact stationary single-agent wealth distribution from the microscopic exchange rules,
(ii) determines precisely for which models and parameter ranges the stationary distribution is exactly a Gamma distribution, and exhibits a counterexample when it is not,
(iii) explains the mechanism by which the Gamma form arises (or fails to arise) directly from the collision dynamics, beyond the level of an empirical fit.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has clarified the picture substantially but not provided a single unified derivation. For model (A2) with uniform saving, the Gamma distribution is known to be a very good approximation that matches the first three moments, but moment calculations (e.g., Patriarca–Chakraborti–Germano-type analyses, and the work "Wealth distribution: To be or not to be a Gamma?", arXiv:1004.5109) explicitly disprove that the exact stationary distribution is Gamma — the fourth moments disagree. Kinetic-theory derivations (Düring–Matthes–Toscani; Matthes–Toscani in Comm. Math. Sci. 7 (2009)) provide Boltzmann/Fokker–Planck-based stationary solutions for several variants and identify regimes with Gamma-like behavior or Pareto tails. Thus the original problem of finding a single general analytical stationary solution unifying all of A1, A2, B, C, D remains only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Wealth distribution: To be or not to be a Gamma?
status_evidence.snippet: The fourth moments are different so the conjecture that the Gamma distribution is an equilibrium solution of this model is wrong.
status_evidence.claim: For the uniform-saving CC model, the exact stationary distribution is provably not a Gamma, though Gamma is a very good approximation.

status_evidence.title: Kinetic models of conservative economies with wealth redistribution
status_evidence.snippet: Boltzmann/Fokker–Planck kinetic analysis of conservative wealth-exchange economies, deriving stationary distributions in various regimes.
status_evidence.claim: Kinetic theory provides partial analytical derivations of stationary distributions in particular wealth-exchange models.

status_evidence.title: Kinetic exchange models of markets - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Models with uniform saving yield a gamma-like steady state; with distributed savings a gamma-like bulk with Pareto tail emerges.
status_evidence.claim: Gamma form arises in some variants and not others, and a fully unified general proof is not standard.
